p: Pender mortally wounded — Lane then Trimble commands. Pender was one of Lee's most promising division commanders. His death was a serious blow. Reported time: July 2 afternoon.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (commander successions)
p.short: Site commander-succession record: Pender mortally wounded — Lane then Trimble commands (the record cites Pfanz First Day p.340)

p: Scales wounded — Lowrance assumes brigade. Reported time: July 1 ~3:30pm.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (commander successions)
p.short: Site commander-succession record: Scales wounded — Lowrance assumes brigade (the record cites Pfanz First Day p.312)

p: Avery mortally wounded — Godwin assumes brigade. Avery dipped his finger in the blood from his wound and wrote: 'Tell my father I died with my face to the enemy.' Reported time: July 2 ~9:00pm.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (commander successions)
p.short: Site commander-succession record: Avery mortally wounded — Godwin assumes brigade (the record cites Pfanz Culps Hill p.232)

p: Jones wounded — Dungan assumes brigade. Reported time: July 2 evening.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (commander successions)
p.short: Site commander-succession record: Jones wounded — Dungan assumes brigade (the record cites Pfanz Culps Hill p.92)

p: Stuart arrives at Gettysburg. Lee reportedly greeted Stuart with 'General Stuart, where have you been?' Stuart had been absent since late June on his controversial ride around the Union army. Reported time: July 2 late afternoon.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (commander successions)
p.short: Site commander-succession record: Stuart arrives at Gettysburg (the record cites Wittenberg p.55)

p: Hampton wounded — Fitz Lee senior present. Reported time: July 3 ~3:45pm.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (commander successions)
p.short: Site commander-succession record: Hampton wounded — Fitz Lee senior present (the record cites Wittenberg p.180)

p: Reynolds KIA — Doubleday assumes corps command. Reynolds shot through the head at the edge of Herbst Woods while directing the Iron Brigade. First general officer killed at Gettysburg. Reported time: July 1 ~10:15am.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (commander successions)
p.short: Site commander-succession record: Reynolds KIA — Doubleday assumes corps command (the record cites Pfanz First Day p.65)

p: Doubleday replaced by Newton — Meade sent Newton to replace him. Meade had lost confidence in Doubleday. Newton transferred from VI Corps to command I Corps. Doubleday was deeply offended and spent years defending his actions. Reported time: July 1 evening.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (commander successions)
p.short: Site commander-succession record: Doubleday replaced by Newton — Meade sent Newton to replace him (the record cites Pfanz First Day p.320)

p: Meredith wounded — Robinson assumes Iron Brigade. Reported time: July 1 ~11:30am.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (commander successions)
p.short: Site commander-succession record: Meredith wounded — Robinson assumes Iron Brigade (the record cites Pfanz First Day p.155)

p: Paul blinded — Leonard assumes brigade (1st succession). Reported time: July 1 ~2:00pm.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (commander successions)
p.short: Site commander-succession record: Paul blinded — Leonard assumes brigade (1st succession) (the record cites Pfanz First Day p.220)

p.short: Site commander-succession record: Leonard wounded — Root assumes brigade (2nd succession) (the record cites Pfanz First Day p.222)

p: Root wounded — Coulter assumes brigade (3rd succession, 4th commander). Four brigade commanders in under an hour — a remarkable succession. Reported time: July 1 ~2:30pm.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (commander successions)
p.short: Site commander-succession record: Root wounded — Coulter assumes brigade (3rd succession, 4th commander) (the record cites Pfanz First Day p.223)

p: Hancock wounded — Hays assumes corps command. Hancock refused to leave the field until Pickett's Charge was fully repulsed. He was carried off still issuing orders. Reported time: July 3 ~3:15pm.

p.short: Site commander-succession record: Hancock wounded — Hays assumes corps command (the record cites Hessler-Motts p.210)
